planting.note: Plant transplants after last frost in rich, moist, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Karwinski's giant sage grows into a very large, shrubby specimen in a single season and needs room to reach full size.

directions: Plant transplants after last frost in rich, moist, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Karwinski's giant sage grows into a very large, shrubby specimen in a single season and needs room to reach full size. Large, velvety, gray-green leaves cover a fast-growing, shrubby Mexican sage that can reach ten feet or more in a single warm season, producing tall spikes of small, rose-pink to magenta flowers with fuzzy, felted calyxes in late fall, a display that arrives just as many other salvias are finishing for the year. Its dramatic, fast growth and late-season flowering make it a bold architectural addition to the back of a large border or a tropical-style planting, though it dies to the ground in all but the mildest winters and regrows from the root each spring in marginal zones. Provide plenty of space, water regularly through the growing season, and cut the frost-killed top growth back to the ground in late winter before new growth resumes.

planting.note: Plant transplants after last frost in rich, moist, well-drained soil in partial shade; Bolivian fuzzy sage is frost-tender and grown as a container plant brought indoors for winter outside zones 9-11.

directions: Plant transplants after last frost in rich, moist, well-drained soil in partial shade; Bolivian fuzzy sage is frost-tender and grown as a container plant brought indoors for winter outside zones 9-11. Large, softly textured leaves set off unusually thick, extravagantly fuzzy, hot-pink tubular flowers with a velvety texture unlike almost any other salvia, blooming over a long season and drawing hummingbirds eager for the abundant nectar in each plush, cushiony bloom. Native to cloud forests of Bolivia, it prefers the cooler, humid, partly shaded conditions of its mountain forest habitat over hot, dry, full-sun exposure, performing best with some afternoon shade and consistent moisture in warmer climates. Water regularly, provide dappled shade in hot climates, and protect from any frost, since it has little cold tolerance outside the warmest zones.

planting.note: Plant transplants after last frost in lean, well-drained soil in full sun; curve-flowered sage is drought-tolerant once established and prone to rot in heavy, poorly drained, or overly moist soil.

directions: Plant transplants after last frost in lean, well-drained soil in full sun; curve-flowered sage is drought-tolerant once established and prone to rot in heavy, poorly drained, or overly moist soil. Slender stems carry narrow leaves and elegant, gracefully curved, deep magenta-rose tubular flowers held in loose spikes through a long summer and fall bloom season, an understated but reliably prolific bloomer that draws hummingbirds throughout its flowering period. Native to dry, rocky slopes in Mexico, it is well adapted to lean, fast-draining soil and tolerates drought once established, making it a good candidate for a xeriscape border or gravel garden where richer, moisture-retentive soil would encourage rot. Water sparingly once established, cut back in late winter to remove any frost-damaged growth, and provide full sun for the best flowering.

planting.note: Plant transplants in spring in lean, well-drained soil in full sun; Ultra Violet autumn sage is drought-tolerant once established and blooms over an unusually long season from spring through fall.

directions: Plant transplants in spring in lean, well-drained soil in full sun; Ultra Violet autumn sage is drought-tolerant once established and blooms over an unusually long season from spring through fall. Fine, aromatic foliage covers a compact, well-branched shrub topped with a near-continuous flush of rich violet-purple flowers from spring through the first hard frost, one of the deepest, truest purple tones among the many autumn sage color selections bred from this exceptionally floriferous Texas and Mexico native. Extremely heat- and drought-tolerant once established, it thrives in the reflected heat of a xeriscape border or gravel garden, drawing hummingbirds and butterflies throughout its long bloom season with minimal care. Shear lightly after each flush of bloom to encourage continued flowering, and cut back hard in late winter to remove old woody growth and rejuvenate the plant.

planting.note: Start indoors 8-10 weeks before last frost and transplant out after hardening off into well-drained, average soil in full sun; Evolution mealycup sage grows taller than most bedding-type salvia farinacea selections, useful for the middle or back of a border.

directions: Start indoors 8-10 weeks before last frost and transplant out after hardening off into well-drained, average soil in full sun; Evolution mealycup sage grows taller than most bedding-type salvia farinacea selections, useful for the middle or back of a border. Tall, sturdy spikes of rich violet-blue flowers with a soft, powdery-white bloom on the calyxes rise well above the narrow gray-green foliage, giving this selection a bolder, more upright presence than the shorter bedding types typically used at the front of a border. Extremely heat- and drought-tolerant once established, it flowers continuously from summer through fall with minimal deadheading, drawing bees and butterflies throughout its long bloom season, and holds up well as a cut flower. Deadhead spent spikes to encourage continued bloom, and treat as a perennial in zones 8-10 or a heat-loving annual further north.
